title: Stalks of the transform are fibre integrals
statement:
Use the Fourier coefficient datum of [def-fourier-set]: distinct primes $p,\ell$, the base field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing the values of the fixed additive character $\psi$. For every noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ with $\ell$ invertible, use the adic category $D^b_c(T,E)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]; its integral objects agree with [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Use the completed and rational pullback and tensor operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For a separated finite-type morphism $f:X\to Y$ of such schemes with a chosen compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{P}Y$ ($j$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $P$ proper), the adic compact-support direct image is $Rf_!=RP_*j_!$ of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] on the completed integral categories, an exact $\mathcal O_E$-linear functor between them by [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction], extended $E$-linearly to $D^b_c(-,E)$ by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].

Let $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $V\cong\mathbf A^r_k$ with $r\geq0$, $V^\vee$ its dual, $W=V\times_kV^\vee$, and $p_1,p_2$ the projections. Let $b:W\to\mathbf A^1_k$ be evaluation. Interpret the Artin--Schreier kernel of [def-fd-kernel] adically using [def-fd-adic-fourier-realization], and write $\mathcal L_\psi$ for the corresponding rank-one $E$-object on $\mathbf A^1_k$. In this coefficient convention the transform means the integral-transform formula of [def-fd-transform] with these adic operations:
$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)=Rp_{2!}(Lp_1^*K\otimes_E^L Lb^*\mathcal L_\psi)[r],\qquad K\in D^b_c(V,E).
$$
Here $Rp_{2!}$ is computed with a fixed compactification $W\xrightarrow{j}\overline W\xrightarrow{P}V^\vee$ of $p_2$; one exists by [thm-nagata-compactification], and $j$ is quasi-compact because $\overline W$ is noetherian.
Let $g=\bar\xi:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to V^\vee$ be any geometric point with $\Omega$ algebraically closed. Put $V_{\bar\xi}=W\times_{p_2,V^\vee}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega=V\times_k\Omega$, let $a:V_{\bar\xi}\to V$ and $q:V_{\bar\xi}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ be the projections, and let $b_\xi(x)=\langle x,\xi\rangle$. Thus $V_{\bar\xi}\cong\mathbf A^r_\Omega$, including when the image of $\bar\xi$ is non-closed. Set $K|_{V_{\bar\xi}}=La^*K$ and $\mathcal L_{\psi(\langle x,\xi\rangle)}=Lb_\xi^*\mathcal L_\psi$.

For an adic object on $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, write $\Gamma_{\Omega,E}$ for termwise pro-etale sections of an integral representative followed by $-\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$, with the scalar-linear action on rational morphisms. Define the geometric derived stalk by $M_{\bar\xi}=\Gamma_{\Omega,E}Lg^*M$ (the adic interpretation of [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback]) and $R\Gamma_c(V_{\bar\xi},N)=\Gamma_{\Omega,E}Rq_!N$, with $Rq_!$ computed by the base change of that compactification along $g$; put $H^j_c=H^jR\Gamma_c$. Then there is a canonical isomorphism, natural in $K$, of complexes of $E$-vector spaces
$$
(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K))_{\bar\xi}\cong R\Gamma_c\bigl(V_{\bar\xi},K|_{V_{\bar\xi}}\otimes_E^L\mathcal L_{\psi(\langle x,\xi\rangle)}\bigr)[r].
$$
In particular for every integer $i$,
$$
H^i\bigl((\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K))_{\bar\xi}\bigr)\cong H^{i+r}_c\bigl(V_{\bar\xi},K|_{V_{\bar\xi}}\otimes_E^L\mathcal L_{\psi(\langle x,\xi\rangle)}\bigr).
$$
The source's $H_c^*(\cdots)[r]$ denotes this compact-support complex and its degreewise formula.

proof.text: Let $h:V_{\bar\xi}\to W$ be $(a,g\circ q)$. A map into $W\times_{V^\vee}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a pair $(x,t)$ with the dual coordinate forced to be $g(t)$, so this fibre product is $V\times_k\Omega$, and $p_1h=a$, $p_2h=gq$, $bh=b_\xi$. In coordinates $p_2$ is the affine-space projection, hence separated and finite type. The spectrum of a field is Noetherian of dimension zero (its only prime is zero). Apply [lem-cbc-compactification-geometry-fibre-bound] over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $V,V^\vee,W$, and over $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ to $V_{\bar\xi}$: all four corners of the square are Noetherian and finite-dimensional, and $\ell$ is a unit because $\ell\ne p$. By [thm-nagata-compactification], $p_2$ has a compactification, since $V^\vee$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Use [def-cbc-compact-support-square] to base change that compactification along $g$. This gives precisely a square to which compact-support base change applies; $g$ need not be finite type or smooth.

source.place: Opening sentence: form the geometric-fibre Cartesian square; verify the compact-support hypotheses

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], $K$ is represented by an integral object $K_0$; no new lattice-existence assertion is needed, since raw rationalization keeps the objects. The integral constructible categories used in the pullback/tensor package and in compact-support base change coincide by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization], with the same completed coefficient sheaf and finite-reduction functors. The integral Artin--Schreier realization [def-fd-adic-fourier-realization] on the noetherian characteristic-$p$ scheme $\mathbf A^1_k$ supplies the lattice $\mathcal L_{\psi,0}\in D^b_c(\mathbf A^1_k,\mathcal O_E)$ of $\mathcal L_\psi$, a rank-one object in degree zero: its defining finite etale torsor trivializes it as the completed free rank-one sheaf. Clause (1) of [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], applied to $b$ and to $p_1$, gives the kernel lattice $\mathcal K_{\psi,0}=Lb^*\mathcal L_{\psi,0}$ and $Lp_1^*K_0$ in $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$; clause (2) gives $Lp_1^*K_0\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal K_{\psi,0}\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$. By the rational-level definition in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the latter represents $F=Lp_1^*K\otimes_E^L\mathcal K_\psi$. Hence $F\in D^b_c(W,E)$ in exactly the category required by the base-change theorem, including its compatible finite-reduction etale-origin witnesses.

source.place: First displayed formula: the integrand belongs to the finite E-stage constructible adic category

proof.text:
Apply [thm-cbc-finite-extension] with $X=W$, $Y=V^\vee$, $X'=V_{\bar\xi}$, $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $f=p_2$, $f'=q$, $g'=h$, input $F$ from Step 2, and the compactification of $p_2$ fixed in the statement with its base change, which is the compactification computing $Rq_!$. Step 1 verifies the scheme and compactification hypotheses (no hypothesis on $g$). Its compact supports are those of the statement; its pullbacks are the strict-tower completed pullbacks $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}},Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], rationalized. It yields the natural isomorphism $Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_{2!}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_!Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}F$ in $D^b_c(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,E)$.
To return to the pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] used in the statement, apply [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] to the integral representatives $F_0$ on $W$ and $RP_*j_!F_0$ on $V^\vee$. The latter lies in the integral category of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] by [lem-cbc-integral-compact-support-uniform-restriction]; objects of that category are derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. This gives natural isomorphisms $\gamma_h:Lh^*F_0\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}F_0$ and $\gamma_g:Lg^*Rp_{2!}F_0\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_{2!}F_0$. In the raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] the components $\gamma\otimes1$ are isomorphisms with inverses $\gamma^{-1}\otimes1$, and tensoring the integral naturality equations with $c\in E$ gives naturality for rational morphisms $u\otimes c$. Hence
$$Lg^*Rp_{2!}F\xrightarrow{\gamma_g}Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}Rp_{2!}F\xrightarrow{\sim}Rq_!Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}F\xrightarrow{Rq_!(\gamma_h^{-1})}Rq_!Lh^*F,$$
natural in $K$. No algebraically closed coefficient field is needed.

source.place: First displayed formula: compact-support base change along the geometric point

proof.text:
The kernel description [def-fd-kernel], interpreted through the integral realization fixed in the statement, is $\mathcal K_\psi=Lb^*\mathcal L_\psi$. Use [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition] on integral representatives and then [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to rationalize its composition isomorphisms and their inverses. Since $p_1h=a$ and $bh=b_\xi$ from Step 1, these give
$$Lh^*Lp_1^*K\cong La^*K=K|_{V_{\bar\xi}},\qquad
Lh^*\mathcal K_\psi\cong L(bh)^*\mathcal L_\psi=Lb_\xi^*\mathcal L_\psi=\mathcal L_{\psi(\langle x,\xi\rangle)}.$$
The kernel integral lattice exists by Step 2. These are composition comparisons for the actual completed pullbacks; the last equality is the definition of the sheaf attached to the pulled-back function. The formula remains valid for a geometric point above a non-closed point because $h$ and $b_\xi$ were defined over its actual field $\Omega$.

source.place: Second paragraph: identify restriction of K and of the pairing kernel

proof.text:
Apply the $\Lambda=E$ clause of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso] to $h$ and the two bounded constructible inputs $Lp_1^*K,\mathcal K_\psi$. Its hypotheses hold by Step 2 and the invertibility check in Step 1. It gives
$$Lh^*F\cong Lh^*Lp_1^*K\otimes_E^L Lh^*\mathcal K_\psi.$$
Substituting the two isomorphisms of Step 4 identifies this naturally with $N=K|_{V_{\bar\xi}}\otimes_E^L\mathcal L_{\psi(\langle x,\xi\rangle)}$. The theorem is applied to completed/rational coefficients, where it asserts the comparison in $D^b_c$, with no unsupported inference from an underived discrete tensor product.

source.place: Second paragraph: expand pullback of the derived tensor integrand

proof.text:
For the pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the shift comparison $Lg^*(M[r])\cong(Lg^*M)[r]$ is the termwise identification on K-flat representatives; by [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison] it corresponds under $\gamma_g$ to the completed shift isomorphism of [lem-cbc-completed-pullback-triangles], and it rationalizes by [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport]. With the transform formula explicitly fixed in the statement (the normalization [r] of [def-fd-transform]), combine Steps 3 and 5 to obtain
$$Lg^*\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)=Lg^*(Rp_{2!}F[r])\cong (Lg^*Rp_{2!}F)[r]\cong (Rq_!Lh^*F)[r]\cong Rq_!N[r].$$
Apply $\Gamma_{\Omega,E}$ to this isomorphism. By [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], termwise sections on the pro-etale site of the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ descend to derived categories and commute with shifts. The subsequent scalar extension to $E$ is flat localization and commutes with shifts termwise; on a rational morphism $u\otimes c$ the action is $c(\Gamma(u)\otimes1)$, whose balancing and composition equations follow from scalar linearity. Thus this evaluation gives $\Gamma_{\Omega,E}Lg^*\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong\Gamma_{\Omega,E}Rq_!N[r]$, exactly the derived stalk/compact-support formula with the meanings specified in the statement, in accordance with [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback].

source.place: Final sentence: insert the shift and identify the geometric stalk with compactly supported fibre cohomology

proof.text: Taking $H^i$ in Step 6 gives $H^i((\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K))_{\bar\xi})\cong H^i(R\Gamma_c(V_{\bar\xi},N)[r])=H_c^{i+r}(V_{\bar\xi},N)$: for the cochain shift, $(C[r])^i=C^{i+r}$ and the differential is multiplied by $(-1)^r$, which leaves its kernel and image unchanged. This is precisely the degreewise interpretation of the source's $H_c^*$ notation. Every factor used is natural in $K$, so the resulting isomorphisms are natural as well.

source.place: Final sentence: take cohomology with the cochain shift convention
